page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical arm64 cores powered by AWS Graviton processors, operating at a clock frequency of 3.3 GHz with 1.0 thread per core. The server includes 384 GB of memory, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio equivalent to 2.0 GB of memory per physical core.

For storage and networking, the instance integrates 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage directly connected to the host hardware. It offers a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps without bundled GPU accelerators. The balance between high core counts and baseline network performance enables rapid data processing across distributed environments.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core density combined with integrated high-speed NVMe storage reduces reliance on external block storage volumes for ephemeral disk operations. Tradeoffs include a lower memory allocation per core relative to memory-optimized instances, requiring workloads to fit within the 2.0 GB per core envelope. The hardware profile suits compute-heavy operations demanding fast local storage, such as log analytics, media processing, distributed database nodes, ETL pipelines, and large-scale software compilation.

This instance profile is suited for compute-heavy applications requiring fast temporary storage, including distributed databases, big data analytics, media transcoding, and high-throughput CI/CD pipelines.
